#221. Apple Perkenalkan iPad Mini Layar OLED, Ditenagai Cip A20 Pro

JAKARTA — Apple resmi memperkenalkan model iPad mini terbarunya yang menghadirkan layar OLED pertama untuk lini seri tersebut. Selain peningkatan layar yang telah dinanti-nantikan, Apple melengkapi model iPad mini baru ini dengan cip Apple A20 Pro terbaru.

iPad mini versi penyimpanan 128GB dan 256GB menggunakan CPU dengan spesifikasi yang lebih rendah (binned CPU) yang memiliki lima inti CPU, dibandingkan dengan enam inti pada model 512GB. Berdasarkan halaman spesifikasi, model dengan kapasitas penyimpanan lebih kecil tersebut memiliki satu inti efisiensi lebih sedikit dan daya NPU yang hanya setengah dari model 512GB. Spesifikasi lainnya sama persis.

Dilansir GSM Arena, model mini yang baru ini mengusung layar OLED Super Retina XDR berukuran 8,5 inci dengan resolusi 2.316 x 1.512 piksel dan refresh rate 60Hz. Menariknya, Apple belum menghadirkan peningkatan ProMotion untuk perangkat iPad terkecilnya ini.

Layar baru tersebut memiliki bezel yang lebih tipis, tingkat kecerahan puncak hingga 1.200 nits, serta tersedia dalam opsi kaca nano-texture untuk mengurangi pantulan cahaya. Perangkat ini mendukung Apple Pencil Pro maupun Apple Pencil (USB-C) standar, serta dilengkapi kamera 12MP dengan fitur Center Stage yang ditempatkan dalam orientasi lanskap.

Yang lebih menarik, Apple memindahkan dua pengeras suara ke bawah layar dan kini menggunakan sistem Acoustic Display. Konfigurasi ini dikabarkan mampu menghasilkan bass yang lebih mantap serta volume yang lebih lantang. Sistem tersebut juga mencakup tweeter khusus yang disembunyikan di antara kaca dan rangka aluminium untuk menghasilkan suara frekuensi tinggi yang lebih jernih.

#222. Disebut Tertipu, WNI ABK Kapal Bawa 1 Ton Ketamin Tidak Jadi Tersangka

Bareskrim Polri mengungkap modus penyelundupan narkotika 1,16 ton ketamin yang dibawa oleh Kapal Tanker MT Global 168.

Wakil Direktur Tindak Pidana Narkoba Bareskrim Polri, Kombes Cahyo Hutomo mengatakan awalnya YCY, selaku manajer kapal MT Global 168, mencari Anak Buah Kapal (ABK) untuk kapal pembawa minyak.

Cahyo menjelaskan ada tujuh WNI bersedia bekerja sebagai ABK di MT Global 168. Namun, mereka tidak tahu muatan kapal yang sebenarnya.

"Dari hasil perkembangan pemeriksaan yang kita amankan waktu itu adalah 8 orang, di mana 7 WNI dan satu lagi inisial YCY itu warga negara Taiwan," kata Cahyo, Selasa (27/10).

Dari hasil pemeriksaan, kata Cahyo, pihaknya tidak menemukan keterlibatan 7 WNI yang bekerja sebagai ABK dengan jaringan narkoba tersebut. Ketujuh WNI itu tidak ditetapkan sebagai tersangka melainkan hanya sebagai saksi.

"Jadi pada saat melaksanakan pelayaran, yang tujuh orang itu tidak tahu karena tujuan daripada tujuh orang itu sesuai dengan permintaan agen yang merekrutnya adalah mengangkut minyak. Sehingga kita tidak bisa menemukan mens rea kepada tujuh orang itu," tuturnya.

Cahyo mengatakan modus serupa kerap dipakai oleh sindikat narkoba jaringan internasional untuk merekrut para awak kapal.

"Modus tersebut biasanya mereka itu merekrut para awak kapal yang usianya sudah tua, sudah masa pensiun. Sehingga bagi mereka kan 'oh ini orang-orang yang perlu uang di masa tua'. Akhirnya mereka rekrut," ujarnya.

Selama pelayaran, kata Cahyo, para ABK juga hanya mengikuti arahan tersangka YCY yang bertindak sebagai manajer kapal.

"Jadi tugas para pelaut itu hanya melaut saja. Sesuai dengan perintah, belok kanan, belok ke kiri, itu tugasnya si manajer kapal, ya. Maka kita tetapkan si manajer kapal sebagai tersangka," katanya.

#224. Luis de la Fuente ‘superstar’: así transformó el Mundial la vida del seleccionador español

El técnico, reconocido como mejor entrenador del año en la gala del Balón de Oro, disfruta una explosión de popularidad gigantesca: “Cuando la gente se da cuenta de que es él, flipa; como una estrella de rock”

Tres semanas antes de conducir a España a ganar su segundo Mundial y transformarse en uno de los personajes más populares del país, Luis de la Fuente recordó lo lejos que había estado de todo esto, este lunes mejor entrenador en la gala del Balón de Oro. El Alavés lo despidió en el otoño de 2012, al poco de comenzar la temporada y comenzaron semanas y semanas de preocupación creciente de parado. “El mes que viene me llamará alguien”, pensaba. “Y llegaba el mes siguiente y no me llamaban”. Pese a las circunstancias, él seguía empeñado en su camino y pasaba los ratos muertos en Lezama, mirando trabajar a Bielsa al mando del Athletic. “Estuve cinco o seis meses viendo los entrenamientos de Marcelo. Tengo todos grabados”, contó la víspera de enfrentarse al argentino, que dirigía a Uruguay.

De la Fuente dejó en la cuneta a aquel viejo maestro que le inspiró en la época más dura de su carrera. Aquel partido sentenció a Bielsa, que perdió el puesto unas semanas más tarde, y supuso un impulso determinante para España rumbo a su segunda estrella. La Roja ya había estado allí, pero el seleccionador, que cumplió 65 años durante la Copa del Mundo, se internaba en un terreno absolutamente desconocido. Nada que ver siquiera con la popularidad que ganó después de la Eurocopa de 2024. “El salto ha sido abismal”, dice una fuente de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF). “Nos llegan entre 10 y 12 peticiones al día para que participe en actos. Podría ir a dos o tres diarios durante el próximo año”.

O quizá no podría llegar nunca a tiempo a los lugares donde se celebraran. “Si antes del Mundial era difícil ir con él por la calle, ahora es imposible”, dice una fuente de Gersh, su agencia de representación. “Cuando la gente se da cuenta de que es él, flipa. El impacto es como el de ver a una estrella del rock”.

Hace un par de meses, tenía una cita con el dentista en el centro de Madrid. Aparcó cerca de la consulta y se dispuso a caminar los pocos metros que le separaban de la entrada. Entonces alguien lo reconoció y De la Fuente se detuvo para atenderlo. Enseguida se formó una pequeña reunión que le impedía avanzar. Firmó autógrafos, conversó y accedió a decenas de selfis, algo a lo que se entrega con cierto entusiasmo. “Déjame el móvil, que a mí me salen mejor”, dice a menudo. Cuando terminó de atender a aquel pequeño enjambre y alcanzó por fin la consulta, había perdido la cita.

El magnetismo se dispara en cualquier lugar. El 9 de octubre viajó en AVE a Valencia a visitar un mural dedicado a la selección española y su triunfo del verano. De nuevo, alguien lo detectó y se formó una cola en su vagón en busca de autógrafos y selfis que no consiguió despachar hasta el final del trayecto. Incluso entonces quedaba algún despistado. Un hombre que viajaba unas filas más adelante se asombró al verlo: “No sabe usted lo que se parece a Luis de la Fuente”, le dijo con cierta timidez. “¡Como que soy yo!”. Y todavía se tomó otra foto.

Las personas que trabajan a diario con él ahora y que también lo hacían antes de los triunfos del Mundial y la Eurocopa se asombran de lo bien que se toma este estallido de atención y cariño. “Lo está disfrutando mucho”, aseguran en la Federación. Incluso cuando le ha hecho perder algunos espacios de libertad, como la caña de aperitivo de antes de comer que le gusta tomar en una terraza y para la que ahora escoge cada vez más una mesa en el interior. “Luis ha normalizado la cercanía”, dicen en su agencia. Y eso provoca que cualquier persona sienta que la barrera entre ellos y el seleccionador es mucho menor que con otras figuras públicas. “El 90% de la gente que se le acerca lo hace para darle las gracias”.

“La gente le para, le toca… y dices: ‘No llegamos”, cuentan en la Federación. Sin embargo, él no se apura. Se detiene con todos, sonríe, posa y hasta termina siempre interesándose por alguien, con quien establece una pequeña charla. “Y piensas: ‘Pero no le des conversación”, dice riendo esta fuente.

Ha seducido tanto al ciudadano de a pie que se lo cruza en cualquier circunstancia vulgar como a responsables de grandes empresas que lo reclaman cada vez más para dar charlas motivacionales y de liderazgo. Aparte del valor de su experiencia gestionando un grupo de élite hasta conseguir los objetivos más altos, desde que lo nombraron seleccionador en 2022, De la Fuente ha mejorado mucho su puesta en escena. Después de sus primeras ruedas de prensa, algunas muy complicadas, dedicó tiempo a repasar y estudiar los vídeos de sus intervenciones. Entre eso y la mejoría de los resultados deportivos, el técnico ha ido ganando aplomo y lo que se ve en público se parece cada vez más a lo que se percibe en privado. “Hasta encuentra el momento para un chiste con el que relajar alguna rueda de prensa”, dicen en la Federación. Varias de las ruedas de prensa previas a las últimas rondas del Mundial comenzaron entre carcajadas de la sala.

#225. ‘It’s the smell of freedom’: Belgrade cleans up after Student List triumph

Binbag-wielding volunteers clear encampment used by thugs to intimidate opponents of deposed government

Student List cleaned up at Serbia’s parliamentary elections. So it was only fitting that the morning after a night of raucous celebrations, the movement’s supporters were gathering, bin bags in hand, at Pioneers Park, opposite the national assembly building in Belgrade.

For the previous 18 months, this small patch of greenery – with its established trees and playground – had been a no-go zone. A pro-government camp known as Ćaciland had taken over the space with convicted criminals living there in white tents, happy to attack journalists, or anyone else who came too close. Police stood by but did nothing to prevent the violence.

On election night, it seemed that thuggery might be on the cards again. Half an hour before the polls closed, large numbers of masked, black-clad men started gathering in and around Pioneers Park. Their intimidating presence gave credence to pre-poll predictions that the governing Serbian Progressive party (SNS) would not hand over power without a struggle.

What happened next took almost everyone by surprise. Shortly after the polls closed – and before any projections of the results had been published – Aleksandar Vučić told supporters at SNS headquarters that they had suffered a comprehensive defeat to the Student List. As cheers rang around the heart of Belgrade, he added that he did “not want unrest” or “anything like that on the streets”.

The riot police stood aside and the barriers blocking access to the area around Pioneers Park were removed. The goon squad made a rapid exit – and Student List supporters joyfully ransacked Ćaciland, setting fire to some of the tents.

But this is not a movement that likes to leave a mess. Over the two years of anti-corruption protests that led to the Student List’s victory, participants have always cleaned up after themselves. So the call went out for volunteers to restore Pioneers Park to something approaching its previous state.

Hundreds of people answered the appeal and joined municipal workers to remove the remains of Ćaciland. Some dismantled the mangled white tents, while others painstakingly cleaned and disinfected the climbing frames, swings and slides in the children’s playground.

Radomir Dalic painstakingly combed over the grass to remove cigarette butts and other rubbish. Apparently relishing his labours, he said he was overjoyed that the park was finally rid of “criminals with violent intentions towards us”.

“Yesterday was a big victory, so today is the smell of freedom,” he added. “We are in garbage, but it’s the smell of freedom.”

Tamara Tomic wore yellow rubber gloves for the occasion – and radiated similar pride in taking part. “Gathering here and cleaning this place just shows that we want to live nicely,” she said. “We want to enjoy the city, enjoy a normal life without violence and without anyone torturing us.”

For now, nobody is asking too many questions about how the Student List will govern. In fact, Serbian voters have taken something of a leap into the unknown – because this is a movement that operates unlike a traditional political party. It has no hierarchy and no leader. Its candidates were chosen by a series of student assemblies, with nominations ranging from academics to athletes, economists to engineers.

The Student List did publish an 11-point plan. Most of these points deal with anti-corruption measures – ironically, the pitch that secured victory in 2012 for Vučić and the SNS. Other commitments include judicial reform, media freedom, affordable housing and improved access to healthcare, with the promise of “a doctor in every village”.

But beyond the domestic priorities – in essence, a clean-up for public institutions – little is clear. The Student List went into the elections without naming a candidate for prime minister, let alone a possible cabinet.

Kurt Bassuener, co-founder of the Democratization Policy Council, said he was concerned about what that might mean when the euphoria of victory died down, and the serious business of forming a government began.

A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day

The thinktank chief added: “I’m hoping that there is a dream scenario plan here – they have portfolios and people who have credibility in particular issue areas and they can hit the ground running. Because the danger of a broad coalition like this is that the fissures will show soon after victory.”

Ilija Srdanović, the candidate ranked first on the Student List, has played down the potential for strife. A cardiologist at the university in Novi Sad, the city where a deadly roof collapse sparked the student protests, he has protested alongside the students since the early days. However, he was keen to emphasise that his ranking on the list did not mean he would become prime minister.

“The student movement is fully democratic,” he said, adding that the aim was to buck Serbia’s history of “creating the cult of personality or leadership”.

The 250 candidates on the Student List were “equal subjects in this struggle”, Srdanović insisted, with “numerous candidates who can be chosen for the prime minister position or any other position”.

But his confidence does little to reassure those who have noticed that the broad spread of views held by Student List candidates could lead to trouble. Despite Vučić’s warnings that a Student List government would impose sanctions on Russia and recognise Kosovo’s unilateral declaration of independence, the movement’s foreign and regional policy remains opaque.

“We have not seen seas of EU flags at demonstrations by students or the marches across Serbia,” said Michael Davenport, a former EU and UK ambassador to the country.

“There are massive policy areas where there is no consensus among the Student List or those have been elected. The approach towards accession to the European Union is not clear, nor is the position with regard to regional issues like Bosnia and Herzegovina and, very particularly, Kosovo.”

Many people are happy to leave these concerns for another day. Vučić and the SNS have fallen – and the cacophony of car horns continued throughout Monday as drivers passed the clean-up crew in Pioneers Park.

One visible symbol of the old regime has been swept away. The Student List voters are hoping more will follow.

#226. South Korea’s GDP growth beats forecasts amid AI boom

Asia’s fourth-largest economy grows 3.4 percent year-on-year amid strong semiconductor demand.

South Korea’s economy grew much faster than expected in the July-September quarter amid booming demand for chips used in artificial intelligence (AI).

Gross domestic product (GDP) expanded 1 percent on a quarterly basis, or 3.4 percent year-on-year, advance estimates released by the Bank of Korea showed on Tuesday.

The Bank of Korea forecast in August that GDP would grow 0.3 percent in the third quarter.

Exports, which account for about 45 percent of South Korea’s GDP, rose 2.3 percent quarter-on-quarter, driven by semiconductors, machinery and electrical equipment, according to the central bank.

Investment in facilities and intellectual property rose 4.1 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively, while investment in construction edged up 0.7 percent.

Despite the robust growth in exports and investment, private consumption fell 0.2 percent.

The latest results put the South Korean economy well on track to achieve its biggest economic expansion in more than a decade.

South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said earlier this month that he expected growth to reach 3.4-3.6 percent in 2026, which would be the strongest performance since 2011, excluding the COVID-19 pandemic.

South Korea’s economy grew 1 percent in 2025, its slowest expansion since the pandemic.

Asia’s fourth-largest economy has capitalised on the AI boom amid a global shortage of memory chips.

South Korea is home to two of the three largest memory chip makers, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, which together control roughly 80 percent of the global market for high-bandwidth memory and 60 percent of the market for dynamic random-access memory.

South Korea’s exports in September surged 83.5 percent year-on-year to $120.9bn, with chips accounting for nearly half of all shipments, according to the Korea Customs Service.

#227. بستانيون تحت الماء.. هكذا يقومون بزراعة الشعاب المرجانية لمواجهة "النينيو"

(CNN) -- مع توقع العلماء أن يشهد هذا العام ظاهرة النينيو التي قد تكون تاريخية، يسافر بيجان حسيني من CNN إلى جزيرة موريا في بولينيزيا الفرنسية لتسليط الضوء على منظمة "بستانيو الشعاب المرجانية" التي تكرس عملها لاستعادة الشعاب المرجانية، وهي جزء من مبادرة رولكس "الكوكب الدائم".

من يوليو إلى أكتوبر سنويًا، وقبل أن ترتفع حرارة الصيف ورطوبته، يقضي فريق المنظمة أيامه في جمع المرجان الذي تمت رعايته لمدة تصل إلى عامين في مشاتلهم، ثم يثبتونه مجددًا على الشعاب المرجانية القريبة.

لكن هذا الموسم يفرض ضغوطًا إضافية، إذ من المتوقع أن تصل ظاهرة النينيو، التي ربما تكون قياسية، خلال بضعة أشهر فقط، ولذلك يأملون في تعزيز الشعاب بقوة من خلال زراعة عدد من الشعاب المرجانية الأكثر قدرة على تحمل الحرارة مقارنة بأي وقت مضى.

يقول تايانو تييهو من فريق "بستانيو الشعاب المرجانية" إن نسبة التغطية المرجانية بلغت 20% عند بدء العمل في تيائيا، أكبر مواقع المشاتل السبعة التي يديرونها في أنحاء بولينيزيا الفرنسية، بينما بلغت النسبة حاليًا ما يقرب من 55٪.

تعمل المنظمة على استعادة الموقع منذ عام 2020، حيث استغرق الوصول إلى هذه المرحلة قرابة 7 سنوات، بما في ذلك تجاوز حدث ابيضاض الشعاب المرجانية الجماعي العالمي في عام 2024.

وتتضمن آلية عمل المشاتل المرجانية جمع أجزاء من المرجان السليم، وربط تلك الأجزاء بحبل، ثم تثبيت الحبال بطاولات تحت الماء. عندما تصبح الشعاب المرجانية ناضجة بما يكفي، تُنقل لزراعتها في الشعاب القريبة باستخدام الإسمنت البحري ومشابك مرجانية مصممة خصيصًا لهذا الغرض.

#232. Skenario Licik Tersangka Pembunuh Istri Siri dan Anaknya di Madiun

Pria di Madiun, Dwi Bagus Martono alias Bagus atau DBM (40) tersangka pembunuhan istri sirinya Dini Hardiyanti (30) dan anaknya AGF (4) dengan keji, disebut membuat skenario licik untuk menutupi kejahatannya.

Bagus yang merupakan lulusan politeknik ternama di Bandung ini disebut menyusun siasat dengan berlagak kehilangan anggota keluarga hingga berujung pada pembuatan laporan orang hilang di kepolisian pada 5 Oktober 2026.

Awal mula skenario ini terbongkar dari kecurigaan keluarga korban Dini yang berada di Bogor. Korban yang biasanya rajin memberikan kabar setiap saat, tiba-tiba terputus komunikasinya secara misterius sejak 20 September 2026.

"Korban selalu berkomunikasi dengan keluarganya yang ada di Bogor. Dan komunikasi ini intens, artinya setiap saat dia selalu menginformasikan korban ada di mana, bagaimana keadaannya, bagaimana kondisinya. Namun komunikasi terakhir itu pada tanggal 20 September," kata Direktur Ditreskrimum Polda Jatim Kombes Pol Roy H M Sihombing di Mapolda Jatim, Surabaya, Selasa (27/10).

Pihak keluarga yang cemas sempat berupaya mencari tahu keberadaan korban melalui tersangka. Namun, Bagus sengaja mengabaikan upaya komunikasi tersebut sehingga justru memancing kecurigaan yang lebih besar.

"Pihak keluarga ini juga sempat menghubungi pelaku, menanyakan keberadaan yang bersangkutan ada di mana. Namun respons pelaku tidak aktif sehingga menambah lagi kecurigaan dari pihak keluarga korban," katanya.

Keluarga korban kemudian berangkat dari Bogor menuju Madiun. Mereka berinisiatif melaporkan hilangnya Dini ke Polres Madiun Kota, pada 5 Oktober 2026.

"Nah dari situlah pihak keluarganya yang di Bogor merasa kok ada sesuatu yang tidak biasanya, komunikasi tapi tidak ada komunikasi. Sehingga yang bersangkutanlah keluarga yang di Bogor ini berinisiatif untuk membuat laporan orang hilang di Polres Madiun Kota," ucapnya.

Untuk memuluskan alibinya, pelaku dengan tenang ikut datang ke Mapolres Madiun Kota saat keluarga membuat laporan resmi. Kehadiran tersangka di kantor polisi tersebut dilakukan seolah-olah sebagai bentuk kepedulian suami yang sedang mencari keberadaan istri dan anaknya.

"Kemudian pada saat dilaporkan ke Polres Madiun Kota, pelaku juga ikut hadir. Sebagai bentuk tanggung jawab dari apa yang dia coba skenariokan," tutur Roy.

Di hadapan petugas kepolisian setempat, tersangka melancarkan cerita bohongnya untuk mengelabui proses penyelidikan. Ia mengarang kronologi palsu bahwa setelah terjadi pertengkaran, istrinya pergi meninggalkannya dan turun di suatu tempat yang tidak diketahui sambil membawa sang anak.

"Jadi akibat dari percekcokan di hotel itu, korban merasa eh dibuatlah skenario bahwa korban meninggalkan tersangka. Kemudian turun di satu tempat berikut anaknya pergi meninggalkan dia," katanya.

Sebelumnya, peristiwa nahas ini bermula saat DBM mengajak Dini dan AGF untuk berwisata ke Telaga Sarangan di Magetan dalam rangka merayakan ulang tahun anaknya, pada 19 September 2026. Namun rencana itu tiba-tiba batal karena tersangka lebih memilih menjemput istri sahnya di stasiun.

Dini dan AGF kemudian diinapkan tersangka di sebuah Hotel di Jalan Dr Soetomo, Kota Madiun, pada 19 September 2026 malam. Sementara DBM memilih menjemput istri sahnya dan pulang ke rumah.

DBM kembali menemui korban di hotel keesokan harinya, pada 20 September 2026, pagi. Keduanya lalu terlibat cekcok yang dilatarbelakangi masalah asmara. Korban disebut cemburu dengan istri sah tersangka. Mereka kemudian saling dorong, hingga pelaku mencekik leher korban sampai tak berdaya.

"Jadi dilakukan oleh suami sirinya karena pertengkaran, karena pertengkaran di sebuah hotel di wilayah Madiun Kota. Terus dibunuh dengan cara mencekik ya, mencekik," ucapnya.

Mendapati korban sudah tak bernyawa, tersangka kemudian memasukkan jasad perempuan itu ke sleeping bag yang disimpannya di kendaraanya. Ia kemudian membawa jenazah DBM dan juga AGF yang masih balita meninggalkan hotel menaiki mobil Mitsubishi Pajero miliknya.

Tersangka kemudian membawa jasad Dini dan AGF yang masih hidup ke rumah orang tuanya di Gang Tentrem, Jalan Doho, Kelurahan Winongo, Kecamatan Manguharjo, Kota Madiun. Setibanya di sana, tersangka memindahkan anaknya itu ke mobilnya yang lain yakni Suzuki Karimun, dan mencekik balita itu hingga tak bernyawa di kursi penumpang.

"Jenazah dibawa ke luar hotel, dan anaknya sendiri pun diperlakukan yang sama tapi beda tempat, di dalam mobil," ucapnya.

DBM kemudian membawa jasad kedua korban ke rumah tinggalnya di Jalan Kunir, Kelurahan Ngegong, Kecamatan Manguharjo, Kota Madiun. Di sana jasad kedua korban disembunyikan di kebun belakang rumah dengan dibungkus sleeping bag dan ditutup terpal. Tersangka memesan gergaji dan alat penggilingan daging.

Pada 22-23 September 2026, tersangka melakukan tindakan keji terhadap jasad istri siri dan anaknya untuk menutupi perbuatannya.

Namun pembunuhan itu terbongkar lewat penelusuran penelusuran CCTV sebuah hotel di Madiun. Lokasi di mana korban dan anaknya terakhir terdeteksi keberadaannya pada 19-20 September 2026.

Mereka juga melakukan penelusuran di sekitar rumah terduga di Kelurahan Winongo, Kecamatan Manguharjo, Kota Madiun. Di sana ditemukan lima pecahan tulang yang mencurigakan.

Lima sampel tulang itu kemudian dikirim ke laboratorium forensik. Dan hasilnya, tulang-tulang itu terbukti merupakan bagian dari kerangka manusia.

Berdasarkan temuan forensik dan pengembangan bukti di lapangan, polisi menyimpulkan bahwa hilangnya korban dipastikan akibat tindak pembunuhan. Petugas pun langsung bergerak menangkap dan DBM di pelariannya di sebuah rumah di Desa Mejoyolosari, Kecamatan Gudo, Kabupaten Jombang, Minggu (25/10).

#234. Protest leaders urge French pupils to keep barricading their schools

Activists say struggle must go on until their ‘maximum’ demands are met over teacher shortages and building repairs

French children should continue to barricade their schools and take part in street protests, a student union said on Monday after the government announced a package of education measures to try to stem the crisis.

“Today we’re at the negotiating table, we’re able to negotiate with the government,” Pierre Sourzat of Les Lycéens told France Info television. “We’re in a power struggle and we still need to call for continued mobilisation to meet a maximum of our demands.”

The government told high school student representatives it would cap some class sizes and review the university application system. But Sourzat said: “We want measures, not half measures.”

More than five weeks after the start of high school blockades in September, the government made the proposals to address the demands of what has become the biggest youth protest movement in years. It has been joined by trade unions and cost-of-living protesters in regular mass street demonstrations on Saturdays.

High school pupils had demanded an end to teacher and staff shortages and for repairs to decrepit school buildings that had collapsing ceilings, mould, broken toilets, a lack of chairs and windows that did not shut.

The education minister, Édouard Geffray, said some schools were so dilapidated they were “not fit” for teaching. He announced a government loan of €4bn to regional authorities to begin repairs.

Responding to complaints of overcrowded classes, Geffray said class sizes for 15-year-olds in the first year of high school would be capped at 28 in the 50% of schools in the lowest-income areas, increasing to all high schools next year. He said more teaching posts would be created and there would be a review of the French baccalaureate system.

The university application platform, Parcoursup, which has been described as opaque and unfair, will be changed in 2027 and replaced by a new system in 2028, according to the government. Parliament will hold a debate on the issue on Wednesday.

The higher education minister, Philippe Baptiste, said 15,000 extra student places would be created in higher education, focusing on vocational courses.

Louis Letoublon, who attended a meeting with the prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, on behalf of Les Lycéens, said: “Bravo to the high school students who have demonstrated. We’ve got something: the government is afraid and knows it must do something and listen to us. “Not all our demands were ⁠met. We’ll go on for as long as it takes.”

Baptiste said the government’s door was “open” for more discussions.

Several children have been maimed or seriously injured in the protests, allegedly by police explosive weapons. Hundreds of children have been arrested and held in police custody.

The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment

The authorities have increased security measures and placed restrictions on demonstrations after France saw its worst day of violence in years on 17 October, with looting, fires and vandalism of state buildings. Curfews have been put in place in certain cities, alongside protest bans. Protest routes were pushed to the outskirts of cities on Saturday when demonstrations passed off largely peacefully.

The interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said there had been a new phenomenon in cities such as Nice and Montpellier at the weekend with ultra-right groups arriving in “organised formations” and targeting protesters. Eleven suspects are to face charges.

In a visit to Marseille on Monday, Emmanuel Macron said nationwide street protests were likely continue, and that the next day of street demonstrations on 31 October would also be a “day of risk”.

The French president said the looting and vandalism seen on 17 October should never happen again. Speaking to members of the police, he said it was “not normal” for the country to be in “such a state of turmoil” six months before a presidential election.

Macron steps down next spring and the far-right leader Marine Le Pen is leading the polls.

Macron said: “We will continue to hold the line. If we all do our jobs well, this movement will subside – because we will address legitimate expectations, and because order will be maintained. But nothing is a foregone conclusion.”

Authorities have admitted to security and intelligence failures that paved the way for the clashes on 17 October.

#237. Sixty Christians killed in Ethiopia’s Oromia region

Church officials say more than 20 people have been injured, while 20 homes have burned down as religious tensions flare.

At least 60 Orthodox Christians were killed in separate attacks on October 20 and 24 in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, church officials reported.

The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church’s holy synod on Monday described the killings as “extremely tragic cruelty and suffering inflicted on our citizens”. More than 20 people were seriously injured and 20 homes burned down in the attacks, it added.

The church said 14 people were killed on October 20 in Gora Silingo, Angada Kebele in Merti district, while another 46 were killed on October 24 in the villages of Tereta, Chole and Birbo in Shirka district. Both districts are located in the Arsi Zone in central Ethiopia’s Oromia region.

The holy synod condemned the killings, saying the attacks violated constitutional protections for life and religious freedom, and threatened Ethiopia’s tradition of peaceful coexistence among different faiths.

It called on government institutions to publicly condemn the attacks, strengthen civilian protection and ensure those responsible are brought to justice.

The church also urged security agencies to provide additional protection to affected communities and take preventive measures against further violence.

The Oromia regional government has pledged to pursue those responsible for the killings.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attacks.

According to media reports, a local official accused a newly formed rebel alliance that includes the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA) of carrying out the attacks. The OLA has previously denied allegations of attacking civilians.

The killings come amid continuing insecurity in Oromia, Ethiopia’s largest regional state and home to some 40 million, where government forces have been battling armed groups for years.

In July, the Ethiopian Human Rights Council reported that at least 432 civilians and four local militia members had been killed in targeted attacks across East Arsi between 2021-22 and June 1 this year.

The holy synod said it would seek discussions with senior government officials to address the security crisis.

It also announced prayers for the victims on Monday and directed Orthodox churches and monasteries worldwide to hold similar services on Tuesday, following the Divine Liturgy.

The church expressed condolences to the bereaved families and called for urgent measures to ensure that its followers could live and worship without fear.

#238. Fue un experimento en los años 50 y ahora es el peor barrio de Madrid: 408 pisos de 40 metros cuadrados casi en ruina

La Comunidad de Madrid aprueba, tras décadas de disputas, la primera fase del derribo de 36 de las infraviviendas de la Colonia Experimental

En Villaverde Alto hay 800 personas que viven en chabolas verticales. Es la Colonia Experimental, una isla abandonada construida en los años cincuenta para alojar provisionalmente a familias procedentes de otras provincias, principalmente de Andalucía y Extremadura. Son 408 pisos del tamaño de una caja de zapatos. Miden de media 34 metros cuadrados, las humedades pintan de negro las zonas comunes, en las paredes las grietas parten a la mitad los edificios, los techos son de dos metros de alto, las calles son barrizales sin asfaltar y las fachadas de los edificios se caen literalmente a pedazos. El Ayuntamiento de Madrid las ha catalogado como infraviviendas porque no reúnen las condiciones mínimas de habitabilidad y los vecinos, aunque ya esperan la primera fase para el derribo y reconstrucción, siguen viviendo un infierno todos los días.

Juan Durán y Manuela Quintana, de 71 y 69 años, viven allí. Manuela nació en la colonia y Juan en el mismo barrio, pero calle abajo. Su casa (reformada) es un lugar bonito en comparación con el resto del edificio. Ellos, suben y bajan todos los días los tres pisos de su bloque, aunque ya no puedan más. Las zonas comunes son dantescas. Los bloques son corralas llenas de humedades y escaleras rotas y desiguales protegidas por barandillas oxidadas del grosor de una rama. La imagen la terminan los tendederos improvisados con cuerdas puestas por los vecinos que van de escalera a escalera. Allí, la ropa y las sábanas de los vecinos adornan y dan un poco de color a zonas en ruinas.

José Luis López es el arquitecto que tutela a los vecinos. Es experto en vivienda pública y ha asesorado a los vecinos del Aeropuerto de Madrid, Orcasitas y Fuencarral, entre otros, con viviendas parecidas a las de la colonia, aunque López es franco: “no hay nada en Madrid parecido a la colonia”. “Es el peor barrio de Madrid” y lo argumenta: Conoce más de 100.000 viviendas públicas de Madrid y no hay ninguna que tenga los portales por debajo de la rasante, cubiertas hechas de material cancerígeno como el amianto y tuberías de plomo. Aunque explica que todavía se mantienen en pie, lamenta que algunos edificios de la colonia “no aguantarían una tromba de agua como la de Valencia”.

En el piso de abajo de Juan y Manuela vive Julia Durán, de 69 años. La casa de Julia solo tiene una ventana minúscula por la que entra toda la luz de la casa. Para ella, la colonia es el “gueto de Villaverde”. Juan, Manuela, Ana y Julia se sientan en el diminuto salón para dar testimonio de lo complicado que es vivir en un piso de 30 metros. “No hay intimidad ninguna”, relatan entre bromas haciendo alusión a lo que uno se puede llegar a imaginar. “Somos pobres”, dice Manuela, que con 69 años sigue limpiando casas para aportar a la única pensión que reciben de su marido Juan.

Julia se levanta entre dolores. Hace seis años se cayó de un muro de tres pisos y se reventó las rodillas para siempre. Se asoma a la ventana que da a su calle sin asfaltar. La imagen es indigna en pleno 2026. Esa calle no es una calle, sino un barrizal convertido en un vertedero de basura y palomas muertas donde las ratas encuentran provisiones. Julia vive además con su nieto de nueve años, que tiene autismo. La basura acumulada en el entorno, las calles sin asfaltar y las condiciones de los espacios comunes hacen que la colonia sea, según explica, un lugar difícil para los niños. El deterioro también alimenta las quejas por el mantenimiento del barrio. Juan José García, de 85 años, vive en la misma calle que Julia y ha pagado 96 euros de tasa de basuras, frente a los 37 euros que ha abonado ella. Misma calle, misma basura, distintas facturas.

La degradación de la colonia no es nueva. Las viviendas fueron construidas por iniciativa de la Obra Sindical del Hogar y, en 1984, pasaron a ser propiedad de la Comunidad de Madrid. La Administración autonómica, a través del Instituto Nacional de la Vivienda y después del IVIMA, las mantuvo bajo un sistema de acceso diferido a la propiedad con obligación de compra. En 1994, el Ivima sacó a la venta la mayoría de los pisos y muchos vecinos acabaron convirtiéndose en propietarios de unas viviendas que ya presentaban deficiencias. Hoy, la mayor parte de los inmuebles pertenece a particulares, mientras que la Agencia de Vivienda Social de la Comunidad de Madrid conserva alrededor del 10% del ámbito.

Ana Alonso, representante de la asociación administrativa de cooperación de la colonia, lleva décadas reclamando una solución. Las primeras protestas se remontan a los años ochenta. Posteriormente, durante el mandato de Alberto Ruiz-Gallardón, los vecinos llegaron a encadenarse en las oficinas del Ivima. En 2017, durante el mandato de Manuela Carmena en el Ayuntamiento de Madrid, el Consistorio aprobó un protocolo para desbloquear la actuación. Tres años después, en abril de 2020, se aprobó el proyecto de reparcelación, pero los trámites no se tradujeron en obras inmediatas. La vía judicial tampoco logró resolver el problema: los vecinos sostienen que el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Madrid dio la razón a algunos residentes, aunque la ejecución de la resolución quedó bloqueada por la complejidad de la actuación.

Ahora, más de tres décadas después de las primeras reclamaciones, la renovación ha dado un nuevo paso. El pasado 19 de octubre, la Comunidad de Madrid autorizó el convenio para acometer la primera fase, que afectará a 36 viviendas y contará con una inversión cercana a los cinco millones de euros. El plan contempla demoler los edificios afectados, construir nuevas casas y realojar temporalmente a sus residentes.

Uno de los principales temores es el económico. A los vecinos se les plantearon 833 euros para afrontar el realojo temporal, una cantidad que consideran desfasada ante el encarecimiento del alquiler. Aunque la Comunidad prevé alojarlos en el entorno de la colonia, los residentes aseguran que en Villaverde cada vez resulta más difícil encontrar un piso por menos de 1.000 euros. En paralelo, la expectativa de renovación ha atraído a inversores, sociedades inmobiliarias y empresas que han adquirido viviendas en la zona y las ofrecen en alquiler por precios que rondan esa cifra. Para familias con ingresos modestos, afrontar la diferencia entre la ayuda prevista y el precio real de una vivienda puede convertirse en un obstáculo insalvable. Juan y Manuela, que ya tuvieron que hacer un gran esfuerzo para comprar y reformar su casa, temen tener que endeudarse de nuevo. Quieren volver al mismo barrio, donde han criado a sus hijos y conservan a su familia, pero todavía no saben cómo podrán pagar el traslado ni dónde vivirán durante las obras.

La asociación vecinal quiere que las instituciones conozcan de primera mano la situación. Alonso propone invitar al rey Felipe VI, a la presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, y al alcalde, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, para que recorran las calles y entren en las viviendas. Quiere que vean los problemas de cerca, más allá de los expedientes y los anuncios oficiales. En la colonia también hay niños que crecen entre la falta de espacio, la suciedad y las dificultades para jugar o estudiar en casa. Y hay vecinos mayores que llevan toda la vida esperando una solución. La autorización del convenio abre por fin una puerta, pero el derribo todavía no ha empezado y el futuro de cientos de familias sigue pendiente de que los plazos, las ayudas y las condiciones del realojo dejen de ser una promesa y se conviertan en una alternativa real.

#239. MNC Sekuritas dan Berdikari MI Gelar Edukasi Reksa Dana di UPN Veteran Jakarta

JAKARTA – MNC Sekuritas bersama Berdikari Manajemen Investasi (MI) menggelar edukasi reksa dana untuk mahasiswa Universitas Pembangunan Nasional Veteran Jakarta (UPN Veteran Jakarta) melalui kegiatan Having Fund 2026 pada Selasa (27/10/2026). Kegiatan ini diawali dengan sambutan dari Deputi Direktur Pengawasan Perilaku Pelaku Usaha Jasa Keuangan, Edukasi, dan Perlindungan Konsumen OJK Jabodebek Andes Novytasary dan Dekan Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis UPN Veteran Jubaedah.

Adapun narasumber dalam kegiatan ini antara lain Asisten Manajer Senior Pengawasan Perilaku Pelaku Usaha Jasa Keuangan, Edukasi, dan Perlindungan Konsumen OJK Jabodebek Deva Ananda Putra, Head of Fixed Income Berdikari MI Enky Qahas, serta Senior Marketing Mutual Fund MNC Sekuritas Wesly Andri.

Dalam sambutannya, Deputi Direktur Pengawasan Perilaku Pelaku Usaha Jasa Keuangan, Edukasi, dan Perlindungan Konsumen OJK Jabodebek Andes Novytasary menyampaikan bahwa generasi muda perlu mengubah pola pikir dalam mengelola keuangan, dari yang sebelumnya hanya berperan sebagai konsumen menjadi pemilik melalui investasi. Ia menekankan bahwa investasi perlu dilakukan dengan pemahaman dan literasi yang memadai agar tidak berubah menjadi spekulasi.

“Reksa dana cukup familiar bagi anak muda, khususnya pemula, karena dapat dimulai dengan dana yang terjangkau dan diakses secara digital. Teman-teman dapat mulai berinvestasi sejak dini, tidak perlu menunggu kaya terlebih dahulu,” ujarnya.

Dekan Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis UPN Veteran Jakarta Jubaedah menyampaikan apresiasi kepada para narasumber, peserta, dan panitia yang telah berkontribusi dalam menyukseskan kegiatan tersebut. Ia berharap bahwa kerja sama antara UPN Veteran Jakarta dan MNC Sekuritas dapat terus berkembang melalui berbagai program edukasi, peningkatan kompetensi, serta penguatan hubungan antara dunia akademisi dan praktisi.

#240. أعراض اضطراب الوسواس القهري..ما عوامل الخطر المرتبطة بهذه الحالة؟

(CNN)-- اضطراب الوسواس القهري هو اضطراب عقلي يفرض على صاحبه أفكارًا وسلوكيات متكررة وخارجة عن سيطرته، قد تعيق تفاصيل حياته اليومية.

من المفاهيم الخاطئة الشائعة الاعتقاد بأن الوسواس القهري يعني مجرد الحرص على الترتيب والنظافة؛ ففي حين قد يكون التنظيف أحد الأعراض، يتمثل الاضطراب غالباً في الانشغال بفعل معين يشعر الشخص بضرورة ملحة لتكراره، بدلاً من مجرد الحفاظ على النظام. كما أن طبيعة الوساوس والأفعال القهرية قد تتغير بمرور الوقت.

بحسب موقع medlineplus التابع لمكتبة الطب الوطنية في أمريكا، لا يزال سبب الإصابة باضطراب الوسواس القهري غير معروف، لكن عوامل مثل الوراثة، وبيولوجيا وكيمياء الدماغ، والبيئة المحيطة قد تلعب دوراً في ذلك.

عادةً ما يبدأ هذا الاضطراب في مرحلة المراهقة أو الشباب، وغالباً ما يتم تشخيص الذكور به في سن أصغر مقارنةً بالإناث.

وتشمل عوامل خطر الإصابة بالوسواس القهري بحسب الموقع، ما يلي:

في بعض الحالات، قد يُصاب الأطفال بالوسواس القهري أو أعراضه بعد الإصابة بعدوى بكتيرية عقدية، مما يُعرف باسم اضطرابات المناعة الذاتية العصبية والنفسية لدى الأطفال المرتبطة بالعدوى العقدية.

قد تختلف أعراض اضطراب الوسواس القهري من شخص لآخر، ولكنها غالباً ما تندرج تحت أنماط أو مواضيع مشتركة محددة.

يشير موقع healthdirect الأسترالي، إلى أنه يتواجد نوعان رئيسيان من الأعراض:

يمكن أن تؤدي الوساوس إلى ممارسة الأفعال القهرية، وتستغرق هذه الأفعال وقتاً طويلاً، إذ يصعب مقاومة القيام بها. كما أنها قد تؤثر على أنشطة الشخص اليومية المعتادة.

غالباً ما تنشأ هذه الأفعال القهرية نتيجة الخوف من وقوع شيء سيء؛ مثل الاعتقاد بأن شخص ما سيموت إذا لم تؤدِّ الصلاة بطريقة دقيقة، أو إذا وطأت بقدمك على شقوق أرضية، أو إذا لم تغسل يديك لمدة 3 دقائق بطريقة محددة، كما قد يشعر البعض بالحاجة إلى التحقق من إطفاء المكواة 20 مرة.

وقد يكون الشخص مصاباً باضطراب الوسواس القهري إذا كانت لديه أفكار وسواسية وسلوكيات قهرية تستغرق وقتاً طويلاً، أو مفرطة وغير منطقية، أو تسبب له ضيقاً أو انزعاجاً كبيراً، أو تتعارض مع حياته الطبيعية وعلاقاته، كأن تتسبب في تأخره عن العمل أو المدرسة.

بتسجيلك، فأنت توافق على الشروط والأحكام الخاصة بنا و سياسة الخصوصية.

#241. Pelatihan BSA Sorot Kemampuan Pemanfaatan Media dan Branding bagi Lurah

Di tengah perkembangan teknologi informasi dan komunikasi, para lurah di DKI Jakarta akhirnya memperoleh tugas yang lebih kompleks. Mereka kini diharapkan mampu memanfaatkan media dalam mengembangkan wilayah dan memberikan pelayanan kepada masyarakat.

Untuk membantu para lurah dalam menavigasi perubahan ini, Pemerintah Provinsi DKI Jakarta melalui Biro Kerja Sama Daerah (KSD) Setda, mengadakan pelatihan untuk 52 lurah dari berbagai daerah di Jakarta.

Tak dipilih secara acak, 52 lurah ini merupakan peserta dari ajang penghargaan Benyamin S Award (BSA) 2026. Ajang penghargaan BSA merupakan platform apresiasi bagi para lurah yang mampu menghadirkan perubahan nyata dan berkelanjutan.

BSA mendorong setiap kelurahan untuk membangun lingkungan yang lebih bersih, nyaman, indah, dan sejahtera, sekaligus menghidupkan semangat Benyamin Sueb dalam perjalanan Jakarta menuju kota global. Pelatihan BSA yang diadakan pada Selasa (27/10) di Paragon Community Hub, selaras dengan visi BSA tersebut.

Melalui pelatihan ini, Biro KSD memiliki harapan agar lurah menjadi garda terdepan pemerintah seiring perjalanan Jakarta menuju kota global.

"[Harapannya] mereka lebih mampu mendeliver seluruh program Bapak Gubernur dan Bapak Wakil Gubernur dalam hal ini Pemerintah Provinsi DKI Jakarta secara baik, secara tepat, dan melayani secara profesional," ujar Kebag Kerja Sama Pihak Ketiga Biro KSD Setda, Faisal.

Pengelolaan media sosial, penentuan pesan, dan pembentukan branding menjadi pembahasan yang kerap muncul dalam pelatihan. Para lurah berpartisipasi aktif dalam diskusi dengan pelatih, dari mulai memberikan pertanyaan hingga membagikan pengalamannya soal topik yang dibahas.

Para lurah pun mengungkapkan kesan mereka usai mengikuti pelatihan di Paragon Community Hub ini. Salah satu lurah yang CNNIndonesia.com temui adalah Jamaluddin, Lurah Pulau Panggang, Kabupaten Kepulauan Seribu, yang menjadi salah satu finalis BSA.

"Alhamdulillah selama saya mengikuti BSA ini, banyak yang saya dapat, termasuk pelatihan-pelatihan yang mungkin ini menjadi modal buat kami di wilayah. Yang saat ini saya ada di kantor Paragon, secara umum saya lihat luar biasa," ujar Jamaluddin.

Soal aktivitas media sosial, sebut Jamaluddin, kelurahan Pulau Panggang pun telah bergerak aktif di ranah tersebut.

Namun, dengan adanya pelatihan BSA ini, Jamaluddin berharap dapat meningkatkan kualitas media sosial yang dimiliki kelurahan. Secara khususnya, mengembangkan branding kelurahan sebagai destinasi wisata.

"Mudah-mudahan sekali lagi lewat [pelatihan] BSA ini Kelurahan Pulau Panggang bisa menggaet wisatawan yang dari darat ke Kelurahan Pulau Panggang," ucapnya.

Sementara itu, Lurah Pluit, Faizal, juga mengungkapkan kesannya setelah mengikuti pelatihan ini. Ia menyatakan bahwa ia merasa terapresiasi karena dapat mengikuti pelatihan walau tidak masuk dalam seleksi 10 besar.

"Tadi juga berkolaborasi dengan Paragon dan jajarannya, bagaimana mereka bisa membangun branding yang kuat, juga bisa memberikan edukasi bagaimana seorang lurah bisa mengangkat wilayahnya," ucap Faizal.

Pelatihan ini juga disebut menyediakan kesempatan bagi Faizal untuk bertukar pikiran dengan para lurah yang masuk ke dalam 10 besar.

"Lurah-lurah yang masuk nominasi 10 besar, bagaimana mereka memberikan apresiasi untuk wilayahnya, lalu juga memberikan tips-tips untuk lurah-lurah yang lain supaya motivasinya terus tumbuh dan berkembang," ujarnya.

Dari 52 lurah peserta BSA, telah tersaring 10 lurah yang masuk ke dalam babak final. 10 finalis ini berasal dari Pulau Panggang, Kelapa Gading Timur, Malaka Sari, Utan Kayu Selatan, Srengseng, Sukabumi Utara, Taman Sari, Kebon Baru, Cilandak Barat, dan Kebon Sirih.

Pemenang dari ajang BSA akan diumumkan dalam acara penghargaan yang digelar 30 Oktober mendatang.

#245. سوريا تغلق منفذها مع الأردن.. ونقابة المحامين تطالب باستدعاء السفير ومخاطبة مجلس الأمن

تتواصل تداعيات الضربات التي نفذها سلاح الجو الأردني مساء أمس في درعا جنوبي سوريا، حيث أغلقت السلطات السورية المنفذ البري الوحيد بين البلدين، مما أدى إلى تكدس مئات الشاحنات على الحدود، بالتزامن مع تصريحات لوزارة الداخلية السورية شددت فيها على "أولوية حماية المدنيين"، في وقت اعتبرت فيه نقابة المحامين السوريين العملية "خرقا للسيادة وترقى إلى جريمة حرب"، مطالبة باستدعاء السفير الأردني في دمشق.

وأعلنت الهيئة العامة للمنافذ والجمارك في سوريا، في وقت متأخر ليلة أمس، إغلاق منفذ نصيب الحدودي مع الأردن، إذ نص القرار على التعليق الكامل لحركة المسافرين والشاحنات التجارية في كلا الاتجاهين "تعزيزا لسلامة المسافرين والعاملين في المنفذ الحدودي".

وعلى خلفية القرار، شهد المعبر منذ لحظة إغلاقه وصولا إلى ساعات صباح اليوم، تكدسا كبيرا لشاحنات البضائع ومركبات الشحن التي كان من المفترض أن تعبر في الاتجاهين بين البلدين.

من جهته، قال المتحدث باسم الداخلية السورية، نور الدين البابا، اليوم الثلاثاء، إن الوزارة تواصل "عملها للوقوف على ملابسات الحادثة عبر التنسيق مع الجهات المختصة".

وأضاف البابا: "وفي الوقت الذي تواصل فيه وزارة الداخلية السورية جهودها في مكافحة الإرهاب وملاحقة تجار المخدرات ومكافحة الجريمة العابرة للحدود، تبقى حماية المدنيين أولوية، ويظل التنسيق بين البلدين السبيل الأمثل لمعالجة التحديات الحدودية دون المساس بأرواح الأبرياء".

بالتزامن مع هذه التطورات، أصدرت نقابة المحامين السورية بيانا عبرت فيه عن "بالغ القلق والاستنكار لما أقدم عليه سلاح الجو الأردني من تنفيذ غارات جوية استهدفت مواقع في ريف درعا". وقالت النقابة إن الضربة الأردنية تمت دون أي تنسيق مسبق مع الجهات السورية، مشيرة إلى أن "استهداف الأراضي السورية دون إذن يشكل انتهاكا صارخا لمبدأ سيادة الدول ولأحكام القانون الدولي وميثاق الأمم المتحدة".

وأضافت أن سقوط ضحايا من المدنيين يرقى إلى "جريمة حرب وانتهاك جسيم لأحكام القانون الدولي الإنساني واتفاقيات جنيف لعام 1949 التي تحظر استهداف المدنيين"، واعتبرت "مزاعم استهداف أوكار إرهابية لا تمنح أي مشروعية قانونية لوقوع ضحايا مدنيين ولا تشكل سندا للاعتداء على سيادة دولة أخرى".

وطالبت النقابة الحكومة السورية باستدعاء السفير الأردني في دمشق وتسليمه مذكرة احتجاج رسمية تتضمن إنذارا شديد اللهجة، ومخاطبة مجلس الأمن الدولي والأمم المتحدة لتسجيل الانتهاك والمطالبة بفتح تحقيق دولي مستقل.

كما دعت إلى تحرك دبلوماسي عبر الجامعة العربية ومنظمة التعاون الإسلامي، والمطالبة بالتعويضات عن الأضرار البشرية والمادية وملاحقة المسؤولين أمام المحاكم المختصة، فضلا عن "تشكيل لجنة قانونية من النقابة لتوثيق الأدلة وجمع الشهادات تمهيدا لاستخدامها في أي مسار قانوني وطني أو دولي".

وكانت وزارة الطوارئ والكوارث السورية قد أعلنت انتشال جثامين 7 قتلى (3 أطفال و3 رجال وامرأة) وإسعاف 3 مصابين جراء القصف الأردني الذي طال 4 مواقع جنوبي سوريا.

كما أكدت الخارجية السورية استنكارها للقصف الأردني في درعا، قائلة إن هذا ‏‏‏‏التصرف الميداني "مرفوض جملة وتفصيلا، ولا يمكن القبول به تحت أي ذريعة، ‏‏‏‏لكونه يمثل خرقا صريحا لمبادئ حسن الجوار والسيادة الوطنية السورية، وينافي أطر ‏‏‏‏العمل والتنسيق المشترك".‏ وتابعت في بيان أصدرته اليوم الثلاثاء، إن سوريا "على يقين تام بأن هناك أطرافا مشبوهة تسعى جاهدة لتعكير صفو العلاقات الأخوية المتميزة بين البلدين"، معلنة العمل "بالتنسيق المباشر مع الأشقاء في الأردن على تشكيل لجنة ميدانية وأمنية مشتركة عاجلة، تهدف إلى وضع حد لهذه ‏‏‏‏الخروقات والتجاوزات الميدانية ومنع تكرارها، وضبط وتأمين حماية الحدود المشتركة ‏‏‏‏بين البلدين".

#246. Palestine weekly: West Bank under siege as Israelis go to the polls

Israel sealed the West Bank, emptied parts of Hebron and tightened the squeeze on Gaza as its election campaign wrapped up.

While Israelis go to the polls this week in one of the most consequential elections in years, many Palestinians in the West Bank have been confined to their homes or neighbourhoods as a wave of Israeli military operations around Hebron continues.

The West Bank city has been in a state of lockdown since two Palestinian gunmen opened fire at an army checkpoint at Hebron’s northern entrance on Friday, killing two Israeli soldiers and wounding three. After the suspects were killed, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the isolation of Hebron and said troops would go house to house in the gunmen’s neighbourhood. “We will act to destroy this place, to change it completely,” he proclaimed.

What followed has been a mass displacement operation in the Hebron area, echoing last year’s military expulsions of three refugee camps, alongside widespread destruction in the neighbourhoods targeted by the army, evoking scenes out of Gaza.

During the weekend, soldiers ordered residents of al-Jalda and Ein Deir Baha neighbourhoods out by loudspeaker, according to residents. Thousands have been forced out of their homes already, with Defence Minister Israel Katz saying people would not be allowed back “until we’ve finished dealing with all the Hamas issues in Hebron”. By Monday, the governorate’s fourth day under closure, at least 3,171 Palestinians from 488 families had been forced out, according to Hebron Municipality data cited by the Wafa news agency. Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said Israeli forces had searched more than 500 homes, arrested more than 70 people and fragmented the city with 128 closed gates and 120 checkpoints.

The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society says the displaced include 127 infants, 81 pregnant women and 26 people with disabilities, and that at least 47 people have been detained in Hebron since Friday.

Bulldozers razed a three-apartment building belonging to Riyad Amrish, as well as a tile and ceramics factory, an auto-parts shop and other businesses in Farsh al-Hawa. Israel’s Channel 12 said Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich ordered the demolitions.

Israeli NGO B’Tselem warned the operation amounts to “collective punishment and acts that could constitute war crimes”.

But Hebron is only the most prominent of multiple sieges happening at different scales, with years-long efforts to strategically encircle Palestinian communities in the West Bank now being employed to devastating effect:

The only Palestinians who can vote – Palestinian citizens of Israel – may face issues at the polls, too; Israel’s Channel 12 reported that Netanyahu’s Likud party was preparing to challenge results from Arab polling stations before a vote had been cast.

This year’s olive harvest has drawn unprecedented levels of settler pogroms, theft and closed-military-zone orders. The Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission has counted 482 attacks on the harvest by Sunday across nine governorates, Wafa reported.

At the same time, Israel released nine of 10 settlers arrested following last week’s attacks on a foreign journalist and diplomats. The attacks have continued undeterred. Wafa reported 17 attacks on farmers and their property on Thursday, and the commission documented 21 in 12 hours on Friday. The past week’s harvest-related incidents fall into a handful of repeating patterns:

Those joining the harvests in solidarity were targeted, too. United States Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was among about 80 volunteers detained near Nahalin on Wednesday and released with a “warning”; Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused him of “harvesting headlines”.

The last week in Gaza saw at least 37 more Palestinians killed as Israel’s daily attacks continued. Monday’s daily report from the Gaza Ministry of Health alone recorded 11 deaths – eight newly killed, three recovered from rubble – and 35 wounded, taking the toll since the October 2025 “ceasefire” to 1,559 killed and 5,608 wounded, with a cumulative toll of 74,555.

For days, hunger worsened with crossings into Gaza shut: Flour stocks ran out, leaving seven of 20 commercial bakeries open, Abdul Nasser al-Ajrami of the bakers’ association told Wafa, and a tray of eggs reached a price of 60 shekels ($19.50).

The pressure began to ease somewhat on the evening of October 23, as Israel told traders that commercial goods would resume and an Egyptian committee delivered flour, Mohammad Abu Warda of the private sector’s emergency committee said.

#247. Israel election live: polls open in most consequential vote in country’s history

Most polling shows Netanyahu’s coalition will lose its majority; suspected stabbing attempt against Democrats’ leader Yair Golan foiled

What you need to know about Israel’s election

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the Israeli elections. Polls have opened in the first election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023, Israel’s subsequent destruction of Gaza, and the launch of its war with the US against Iran.

Most polling shows prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition will lose its majority in the 120-seat Knesset, but the opposition bloc will probably also fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government.

For Netanyahu, 76, who has led the most far-right government in Israel’s history, the stakes are both political and personal. He is on trial for corruption in three separate cases, despite interventions from Donald Trump, who called for a pre-emptive pardon in the long-running saga and even wrote to Israeli president Isaac Herzog on Netanyahu’s behalf. The cases are ongoing.

It was on Netanyahu’s watch that Hamas militants broke out from Gaza three years ago to kill nearly 1,200 people, the majority of them civilians, on the deadliest day in Israel’s history. This election is widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership since those attacks.

The IDF’s globally condemned assault on Gaza, which has killed at least 75,000 people and been deemed a genocide by a UN commission, academics, legal scholars and Israeli and international rights groups, has left Israel a pariah on the world stage.

Three years of regional conflict followed the 7 October attacks, including this year’s war on Iran, which sparked an ongoing global energy crisis and has killed thousands of people, mainly in Lebanon and Iran.

What is more, under Netanyahu’s government there has been an unprecedented, aggressive surge of deadly extremist settler violence to bolster Israeli control in the occupied West Bank, as settler militants and their political backers – who have propped up Netanyahu’s government – exploited their seat at the cabinet table and expanded with impunity.

Indeed, settlement expansion has been a key feature of Netanyahu’s re-election campaign. However, it is also a driving force behind Israel’s growing international isolation, with many of its traditional allies condemning “settler terrorists” and announcing plans to impose sanctions.

In an earlier post, we mentioned that, as of 10am local time, turnout in the Israeli general election was at its highest point at that stage of voting since 1981.

We now have some more figures from the Central Elections Committee, which appear to confirm the trend, with the new data showing that 31.5% of Israelis voted by noon, the highest voter turnout by midday since 1977.

In the settlement of Efrat near Jerusalem, Shani, 19, had come to the polling station with her parents, to cast her vote for the far-right party of finance minister Bezalel Smotrich.

She is part of a large cohort of first-time voters who are more rightwing than older generations, and may help bolster support for Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition partners.

More than 500,000 Israelis have reached voting age since the last election in 2022, and three-quarters of first-time Jewish voters define themselves as right or centre-right, a recent poll for Channel 12 television found (it did not survey Palestinian citizens of Israel).

Shani said she chose Smotrich, a settler himself, for his promises to expand Israel’s footprint in occupied Palestine. “Smotrich is pushing forward with settlement expansion and improving security,” she said.

Her mother, kindergarten teacher Rivka, also voted for Smotrich, and said her priority was to return Netanyahu’s coalition to office.

“The right must win, because otherwise there is a chance of a Palestinian state, which will be very bad for Jews,” she said. Her husband Motti, who runs a healthcare standup had voted directly for Netanyahu. “He’s a diplomat, he’s strong. He’s got whatever leadership should have.”

Spiralling attacks by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinians, and the growing threat of sanctions on settlement goods and construction, were not a key election issue for voters in Efrat who spoke to the Guardian.

Software engineer, Yitzchak Schwarz, 36 is an activist for far-right libertarian Moshe Feiglin, running on a joint slate with Smotrich for this election. “If there are sanctions, it’s going to hurt a bit, but we have to think about our own survival and our own national rights,” he said.

Sue and Tom Rosenfelt, who have lived in Efrat for over 30 years and have three sons in the reserves, said national unity and the unequal burden of military service are their main concerns. “I think that at this point getting another foothold and another hilltop isn’t the thing that’s going to strengthen the country as a whole,” Tom said. “We need to work more on unity.”

In an election which many Israelis describe as critical, turnout was so high at their polling station at a school in Efrat that they had left the long lines, and planned to come back later.

Both plan to vote for the party of Naftali Bennett, a rightwing settler and tech multimillionaire, who joined forces with centrist Yair Lapid. “I feel like this is a time when we need to come together,” Sue Rosenfeld said. “You know, Bennett and Lapid are on different sides of the spectrum, but they’ve come together and that’s something I want to support.”

There has been a suspected attempted stabbing of the leader of the Democrats party, Yair Golan, at HaMesila park in Tel Aviv, the party has said in a statement.

During a voter mobilisation tour, the party said “an unidentified man wearing a jacket” approached Golan in a “threatening manner”.

double quotation markGolan’s security guards blocked the man, and as they moved toward him, a large knife slipped from beneath his clothing and fell to the ground. The security guards immediately subdued him before he could do anything. Police were called to the scene and arrested the suspect.

“Incitement and violence will not deter us. This is the direct result of the poison machine operated by Netanyahu and his Qatari agents. I call on everyone who cares about security and democracy to go out and vote now, so that we can ensure the country we love so dearly becomes a free and safe place once again.”

Golan fought a long legal battle to get security protection from the Shin Bet security service. They only resumed responsibility for his security on Monday, the day before the elections.

While the media attention has been focusing on the country’s parliamentary elections, Israel’s assault on Gaza has continued, a year after the signing of a so-called ‘ceasefire’ with Hamas.

A UN commission said yesterday that Israel was continuing to commit genocide in Gaza despite the signing of the US-brokered ceasefire last October.

The ​report by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel, rejected a claim in May by Donald Trump’s Board of Peace that the truce had “largely held”.

It said Israeli authorities had kept committing “genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole ​or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza”. The report said:

double quotation markThe perception of Palestinians and a possible Palestinian state as a threat to Israel and the desire to reduce the Palestinian population contribute to a permissive military culture where Israeli soldiers, with or without directives from commanders, directly target Palestinians whether or not they pose a real or immediate threat.

Testimonies by Israeli soldiers in Gaza display a disregard for Palestinian lives and a military culture where Palestinians are dehumanized, equated with “terrorists”, trivializing the killing of civilians.

The report noted that between the 10 October ceasefire in 2025 and 30 September 2026, Israeli attacks killed at least 1,431 Palestinian people in Gaza, including 300 children and 130 women.

In its latest update, Gaza’s health ministry said that 74,561 Palestinian people have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza since October 2023, when Isreal launched its assault on the territory following the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed.

The report also accused Israeli forces of having committed crimes against humanity in the West Bank. It lists extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence. Israel has dismissed the findings of the report and has denied committing genocide in Gaza.

Benjamin Netanyahu, who is fighting for his political survival, has just cast his ballot in Jerusalem.

In a post on X this morning, the Israeli prime minister wrote “right-wing voters, this is an emergency hour” as he urged them to get out and vote to counter any left electoral gains.

“Higher-than-usual turnout rates in the left’s strongholds. Right or Palestine, for real,” Netanyahu wrote.

Police believe the arrest of three people in southern Israel who are suspected of being involved in voting bribe attempts was a single incident and not part of a larger campaign, according to Dean Livne, acting director-general of the Elections Committee.

Citing figures released by the Central Elections Committee, the Israeli newspaper Ynet is reporting that voter turnout in the election reached 16.68% by 10am local time (8am GMT), the highest level recorded at that hour since 1981.

Over 1.2m Israelis had cast their ballots by 10am, according to the data, a rise of 0.78 percentage points compared with the same stage of the previous election in 2022.

In Sanhedria cemetery in north Jerusalem, ultra-orthodox voters came to the tombs of revered rabbis before they cast their ballots. There was no question of which way they were going to vote: for the parties representing Ashkenazi and Sephardic ultra-orthodox. But some at the Sanhedria cemetery, the young especially, made clear they only would do so reluctantly.

Yair Shuker, aged 19, said only one issue was important to him. “The election is about whether we will live by the Torah, or there will be no Torah. There will be a Jewish state or there will be no Jewish state,” he said.

And for him - as with almost all Israel’s ultra-orthodox (the Haredim) - the critical measure of the state’s level of observance is whether the Haredim would continue have exemption from military service.

“There are some who study the Torah, and some who stand and defend the land,” Shuker said.

The exemption for ultra-orthodox religious students dates back to the founding the state, but has long been a sort of tension among Israeli Jews, all the more so since the 7 October attack in 2023 and the start of the Gaza war. Israel’s supreme court ruled in 2024 that the blanket exemption for haredi men had no basis in law.

In return for their support in keeping him in power, Benjamin Netanyahu promised the ultra-orthodox parties (the Sephardic party Shas and the Ashkenazi United Torah Judaism) new legislation that would perpetuate the exemption, but has failed to deliver on that promise due to splits in his coalition. As a result both parties left the government, though Shas remained part of the coalition.

Whatever their feelings about Netanyahu, both would vote against a secular-led government led by the current opposition parties, which have pledged to end the exemption once and for all, and enforce military service if necessary.

Shuker said he did not trust either coalition, but would vote because he had been told to. “The rabbi has asked us to vote for Shas, so I will vote,” he said. A 23-year-old Ashkenazi ultra-orthodox, who identified himself as Yaacov K, expressed the same sense of disillusion mixed with duty. He said:

double quotation markI’ll tell you the truth. To me and most of the people around me, we don’t believe in anyone.

If you’re asking me, I’ll never go and vote. But I have a rabbi and the rabbi told me listen, you have to go and vote. And if he says you have to go and vote, then that’s what I do. I don’t even start thinking if it’s worth it for me or not worth it for me.

The open distrust and contempt for Netanyahu, coupled with obedience and party discipline, could be one reason that the prime minister’s bloc has over-performed by a seat or two in past elections, compared to his poll numbers. That could be crucial if the pattern is repeated.

Azriel Zadok, a rabbi who had come for morning prayers at the Sanhedria cemetery, argued that the mass ultra-orthodox vote was essential to preserve Israel’s Jewish identity from “the left”.

“We have no problem with the secular. We pray for them, and we pray for the soldiers,” Zadok said. “Our problem is with the leftists we are trying to decide for us how we should live.” “They want us to go to the beach on Saturday and they want us to marry outside our faith. We want to remain Jews,” the rabbi added.

The centre left is only a small part of the opposition bloc, and it does not propose to change the ultra-orthodox lifestyle. But the bloc is united on the insistence that the Haredim should do their part in the defence of the nation. It is the most divisive issue among Israeli Jews voting today.

According to Israel’s Hareetz newspaper, United Arab List (Ra’am), an Islamist party headed by Mansour Abbas, has filed a complaint to the Central Elections Committee, alleging that a systematic campaign has been launched to disrupt voting for the party.

In a statement, the party said police arrested several of its leading activists in southern Israel’s Negev region before dawn with no clear justification, according to Hareetz.

The party also said there is a widespread shortage of its Arabic-language ballot slips in several areas, including the cities of Nazareth and Shfaram in northern Israel. We have not yet been able to independently verify these claims.

About 15 million people live in areas under Israeli control. Just over 7 million Jewish Israelis and 1.7 million Palestinian citizens of Israel live within the country’s pre-1967 borders, known as the “green line”, and have full voting rights.

In the occupied West Bank, more than 500,000 Israeli settlers can vote. They live among 3.1 million Palestinians who are subject to military rule and do not have the right to vote.

In occupied East Jerusalem more than 230,000 Israelis with voting rights live among 350,000 Palestinians who cannot vote.

Two million Palestinians in Gaza, who live under Israeli military occupation, according to the international court of justice, also have no vote.

The Knesset, the Israeli parliament, has 120 seats, with lawmakers voted in through a system of proportional representation. No single party has ever claimed a majority of 61 seats, so Israel has always been governed by coalitions.

When the results are in, the president invites the party with the largest number of seats to try to agree a governing coalition. Exit polls are released at 10pm Israeli time (8pm GMT), and the first indication of actual voting counts usually emerges in the early hours of the morning.

Getting full results could take much longer, with the outcome potentially hanging on the electoral fortunes of two small parties, which need to win 3.25% of the overall vote to take up seats in the Knesset. Polling puts both around this threshold. If they cross it, they each get four seats, which would have a significant impact on coalition building options.

The far-right Amcha Yisrael is led by the former general Ofer Winter, who has pledged to back Netanyahu for prime minister if he gets into the Knesset. The Reservists is a rightwing Zionist party focused on ensuring universal conscription whose leaders sit between the two blocs.

They have ruled out joining any government supported by either the ultra-Orthodox – key Netanyahu allies – or Palestinian parties whose backing Gadi Eisenkot is likely to need. If it goes down to the wire, counting could take more than a day.

Palestinians with Israeli citizenship constitute about a fifth of the population but are consistently under-represented in the parliament.

Benjamin Netanyahu and most of his chief rivals have said they won’t form a coalition with parties (broadly) representing Palestinian citizens of Israel - even if that means political gridlock.

But after the votes are counted these parties could hold a critical balance of power, as my colleagues Emma Graham-Harrison and Quique Kierszenbaum highlight in this story. Here is an extract from their report:

Palestinian citizens of Israel are forecast to secure between 12 and 15 seats, divided between the Islamist Ra’am and the Joint List alliance of three smaller parties, Hadash, Balad and Ta’al.

The mathematics of power are clear, even though most of the Jewish Israeli opposition has ruled out a coalition with Arab politicians, and Netanyahu and his allies have been doing everything they can to make such an alliance politically toxic.

There is recent precedent for breaking promises not to work with Palestinians, however. The Ra’am leader, Mansour Abbas, in 2021 took his party into a historic coalition government with Naftali Bennett, now part of the opposition bloc, and Netanyahu himself had previously started coalition negotiations with Abbas.

One prospective voter, Mohammed, works at a hi-tech company, managing both Jewish and Arab employees, which he sees as a template for a different future for Israel.

Although disappointed that most Jewish Israeli opposition parties have ruled out a coalition with Palestinian parties, he understands the political logic, and he expects their position to shift once results are in.

“At the end of the day, everything is mathematics, right? One plus one is two. They cannot do anything without [those seats]. So they must do [some kind of deal] and they will do it.”

A consistent majority of Israeli polls show prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s current coalition bloc with the ultra-Orthodox and the far right will fall below the threshold of 61 seats needed to form a government.

But even though there is a clear anti-Netanyahu majority, polls indicate that the Jewish Israeli opposition bloc will also fall short of the required seats, meaning weeks or even months of political wrangling may be in store as parties make deals and trade concessions.

So who are Netanyahu’s leading rivals in the race?

As we have mentioned in a previous post, the man leading the field to potentially replace Netanyahu, Gadi Eisenkot, is a former head of the Israeli military who formulated the notorious Dahiya doctrine of using “disproportionate force” to cause damage and destruction.

Naftali Bennett is a former prime minister and former chair of the settler council, who supports annexing much of the West Bank.

Avigdor Lieberman wants to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and replace it with an Israeli-Jordanian confederation (though apparently he did not consult the Jordanians about this plan).

The Democrats, the only remaining political home for Israel’s Zionist left, are led by Yair Golan, a former general and deputy head of Israel’s military.

#248. 2 Tim Super League 2026-2027 Belum Terkalahkan hingga Pekan Ketujuh, Bukan Persija Jakarta!

JAKARTA - Super League 2026-2027 telah memasuki pekan ketujuh. Hingga pekan ketujuh, terdapat 2 tim yang belum pernah menelan kekalahan.

Super League 2026-2027 berjalan sengit hingga pekan ketujuh. Juara bertahan Persib Bandung masih tertahan di urutan keempat klasemen sementara musim ini. Peringkat kedua dihuni Dewa United dengan mengemas 14 poin. Yang menarik, tim peringkat 2 hingga 5 hanya dipisahkan 1 poin.

Sementara Persija Jakarta yang kini diasuh Shin Tae-yong mampu memimpin klasemen sementara. Klub berjuluk Macan Kemayoran itu melaju sendirian di puncak klasemen dengan koleksi 18 poin.

Namun, tim yang kini menduduki 5 besar tersebut bukan tidak terkalahkan. Persija, Dewa United, Bali United, Persib Bandung, dan Madura United telah pernah mengalami hasil pahit.

Di sisi lain, tim yang belum pernah kalah justru berada di luar 5 besar klasemen sementara. Kedua tim tersebut adalah Persita Tangerang dan Bhayangkara Presisi Lampung FC. Persita Tangerang yang baru memainkan 6 pertandingan mengemas 12 poin hasil 3 kali menang dan 3 kali seri.

Klub berjuluk Pendekar Cisadane itu berhasil memaksimalkan laga kandang. Dari 4 laga kandang musim ini, Persita meraih 3 kemenangan dan sekali seri.

Satu kemenangan di antaranya bahkan diraih saat menjamu Persija Jakarta yang kini memimpin klasemen sementara Super League 2026-2027. Tim kuat lainnya, Bali United yang kini menempati peringkat 3 klasemen sementara mampu ditahan imbang.

Pada laga selanjutnya, Persita Tangerang akan bertandang ke markas Persik Kediri. Melihat kondisi kedua tim saat ini, bukan tak mungkin Persita Tangerang bisa mencuri poin alias tidak kalah.
